# Add images for all cards

## Problem Statement

The Main Street card redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN) reserves a 64×64 left-art graphic zone on every card face, but all 162 cards currently display only a placeholder (synergy-coloured rectangle with a single-letter initial). Images must be generated from the `art_notes` descriptions in `card-data.csv`, packaged as PNGs, and embedded into the SVG card rendering pipeline so they appear alongside the card text.

## Users

- **Players**: See distinctive, thematic imagery on every card face in their hand, on the street, and in the market — improving recognisability and atmosphere.
- **Developers**: Have a reproducible image-generation pipeline that produces one PNG per card from `art_notes`, with a safe fallback to a generic placeholder when no image exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card across all families (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff) has an associated 64×64 PNG image file in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
2. Images are named `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`) and are referenced by the SVG card generator, which attempts to embed the corresponding PNG and falls back to a generic placeholder when the file is missing.
3. The `graphicZoneSvg()` function in `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` is updated to embed `<image>` elements for the PNG assets (with a fallback `<rect>` + glyph when the image is unavailable or fails to load).
4. All 162 card entries in `card-data.csv` have an `art_notes` value — cards that previously had none receive a generic placeholder description.
5. The full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Image generation quality**: AI-generated images may not match the intended aesthetic. Mitigation: producer reviews images before committing to the repo; a script to regenerate is preferred over manual editing.
- **SVG `<image>` fallback reliability**: SVG `<image>` elements do not gracefully handle missing files — the zone may render blank. Mitigation: the SVG generator emits the `<image>` element, and when the file is absent, falls back to the existing `<rect>` + glyph placeholder.
- **Licensing**: Generated images must be clearly documented as CC0 / self-authored. Mitigation: update `CREDITS.md` with provenance for every new asset directory.
- **Scope creep**: "Every card" could imply artwork for other example games (Golf, Lost Cities, etc.). Mitigation: scope is strictly Main Street 162 cards.

## Constraints

- Images must be permissive / freely available for commercial use (CC0, MIT, or self-authored).
- The naming convention must be deterministic from the card id so the SVG generator can derive asset keys at runtime without additional configuration.
- SVG `<image>` elements must have proper fallback handling so missing assets do not break rendering.
- The 64×64 zone is at `(8, 8)` on the 140×80 card canvas, so images must fit within that rect.

## Existing State

- `public/assets/cards/` — 52 standard playing-card SVGs (CC0, saulspatz/SVGCards) + 1 card back.
- `public/assets/cards/alternative/webisso/` — 52 playing-card SVGs (MIT).
- `public/assets/cards/lost-cities/` — 61 Lost Cities SVGs (MIT).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — 162 rows; 157 have `art_notes`, 5 are empty.
- `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `graphicZoneSvg()` produces a coloured rectangle + initial glyph; comment notes: "Future work can replace the `<g>` body with a real `<image>` or family-specific icon."
- No 64×64 card art images exist anywhere in the project.

## Desired Change

1. Populate `art_notes` for the 5 cards that currently have none (use a generic placeholder description).
2. Generate 64×64 PNG images for all 162 cards from their `art_notes` descriptions, naming them `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`, `comm-library_64_x_64.png`).
3. Place images in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
4. Update `graphicZoneSvg()` to optionally embed an `<image href="...">` element inside the 64×64 zone, with a `<rect>` + glyph fallback.
5. Update the SVG generation pipeline so the asset key is derived from the card id at runtime.

## Key Files (delivered layout, verified 2026-09-29)

- `src/card-data.csv` — card rows; all 173 rows carry an `art_notes` value
- `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` — producer-supplied source art (1024×1024)
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — builds the art map from the CSV and sprites
- `src/card-art-map.json` — generated card-name → embedded 256×256 WebP `data:` URI map
- `src/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — runtime resolver (`getCardArtDataUri`, `resolveCardArtName`, `hasDedicatedCardArt`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `graphicZoneSvg()` embeds the clipped `<image>` with a `<rect>` + glyph fallback
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — pending-aware drift guard (`PENDING_ART_TARGETS`, baseline 78)
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — artifact provenance to update when the new sprites land

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN** — Redesign all Main Street cards with 64×64 left-art (created the placeholder zone).
- **CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA** — Add synergy icons to Main Street help panel (complementary asset work).
- **CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 — Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (mentions placeholder-to-final art pipeline).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Image format? — **Answer (producer):** PNG files.
- Q: How will images be created and named? — **Answer (producer):** Producer will provide images; naming convention `<card_name>_64_x_64.png`, derived from card id. Placeholder used if image not found.
- Q: Scope — all card families? — **Answer (producer):** Every family (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
- Q: Placement approach — SVG or external Phaser assets? — **Answer (producer):** Embedded in SVG.
- Q: Cards without art_notes (5 cards)? — **Answer (producer):** Create art_notes; use a placeholder description.

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshChallengeTracker`) renders the challenge panel as compact rows: indicator + title + description, with a `Challenges (n/N)` header. There is currently no per-challenge progress display.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps every challenge template 1:1 to a persistent Steam achievement; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- Add an `economic` challenge category and the `ch-serial-seller` template with an evaluator counting sold street businesses and an optional progress provider.
- Add an optional `progress?: (state: MainStreetState) => { current: number; target: number }` field to the `Challenge` interface and render it in the challenge HUD tracker (e.g. `2/3`), leaving progress-less challenges visually unchanged.
- Add the `serial-seller` achievement mapping and create the blocking dependency work item for the `core` manifest entry + Steamworks API name.
- Update the affected tests (template count, evaluator/selection/progress/undo, achievement mapping) and documentation.

Design note: keeping progress as an **optional Main Street-specific** field on `Challenge` (rather than extending the generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` in `@core-engine`) keeps the change surgical and avoids touching the core engine. If a second progress-capable challenge is added later, promoting the field to the generic interface can be revisited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add `economic` to `ChallengeCategory`, add optional `progress` to `Challenge`, add the `ch-serial-seller` template (evaluator + progress).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render progress in `refreshChallengeTracker`.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` — add `'ch-serial-seller': 'serial-seller'` to `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`.
- `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — update template count (12 → 13); add evaluator, selection, and progress-metadata tests.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` — mapping completeness/drift now includes `serial-seller` (green once the child manifest entry lands).
- `tests/main-street/` challenge-HUD/scene test — add progress-rendering coverage (extend an existing scene/HUD test or add a focused one).
- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — **blocking dependency** `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (core submodule): add the `serial-seller` entry with `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and/or `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — document the new challenge/category if the challenge catalogue is described there.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — only if the progress indicator requires a layout constant tweak (avoid if possible).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Cross-repo achievement dependency (blocking, build impact).** The manifest lives in the `core` submodule and the drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) fails the build until the dependency (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`) lands and the submodule pointer is bumped. Sequence the dependency first; this item must not reach `in_review` ahead of it.
- **Test friction from template count.** Several tests derive from `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES.length`; only `challenges.test.ts` hardcodes 12. Keep the category-coverage list at the original 5 so `economic` is not required to have ≥2 templates (scope creep risk — do not add a second economic challenge here; capture as a separate linked work item).
- **Undo semantics.** Because completion is flagged on the `ActiveChallenge` and also recorded in `challengesCompleted`, redo must not double-add. Existing per-action reset (`completedChallengeIds.length = 0`) already guards this; add regression coverage.
- **Progress layout.** The challenge rows are compact; a progress suffix must not overlap the description column. Verify at the shipping HUD width.
- **Assumption:** `soldSlots` true-count is the intended "businesses sold" metric (confirmed by producer, Q6 = a). If a future non-street sell path should count, a state counter will be needed — out of scope.
- **Assumption:** final player-facing text is title **Serial Seller** and description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game." (producer-confirmed Q7 update); the `economic` category keeps the original 5-category coverage assertions intact.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding more economic challenges, changing reward points, adding new achievement art, or counting hand/legacy sells are out of scope; capture as linked work items.

# Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw)

**Summary:** Add the engine logic for the Investor's free market re-roll: per-turn state tracking, the bias-aware draw algorithm, and the integration with the existing market refill path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform one coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it advances the per-turn escalation counter (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a 75% chance to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space synergyTypes; event targetSynergy/effect; staff allowedBusinessTypes overlap with the hosting business's synergy types).
- The biased draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed produces same-game determinism.
- `refillSingleRowMarket` is parameterised to accept the bias/relevance pool; the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- The bias draw preserves the >=1-business row composition invariant.

**Parent Coverage:** Implements parent AC2 (One free re-roll per turn) and parent AC3 (Relevance bias).

**Minimal Implementation:**
- Add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` to state types
- Reset flag at `WeekStart`
- Implement `canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`
- Implement bias-aware draw in `refillSingleRowMarket`
- Wire up the bias detection (hosting business synergy types overlap)

**Dependencies:** Add Investor card to catalog (CSV + types + parsing)

**Deliverables:** Engine functions, state field, bias draw algorithm, WeekStart reset.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`

**Summary:** Add a player-facing "move staff" action that relocates a hired staff member from one business to another, consuming 1 action point. The initial placement at hire time remains action-free.

# Intake Brief: Re-tune Reputation Sources for the Slower-Coin Economy (Medium Loss Mode)

**Work item:** MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 (Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns)
**Recommendation R2:** [further-balancing-recommendations.md §5](docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md)

## Headline

After the five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3) reduced business
`baseIncome` by ~2.4×, **reputation collapse became the dominant Medium loss
mode — 69% of losses vs. 30% bankruptcy** (was bankruptcy-dominated). The
economy now produces fewer surplus coins to convert into reputation via
Community Favour, while passive business `reputationPerTurn` was left
unchanged. This task re-tunes reputation sources so the Medium loss-mode split
returns to the PRD design-intent band (reputation collapse 20–40% of losses,
bankruptcy 40–70%) while keeping the win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`.

## Problem statement

The five-turn payback rebalance deliberately tightened the economy (producer
decision Q3 = C, MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3), leaving net liquidity slack (2–4
coins/turn) but starving the reputation economy: with base incomes ~2.4× lower,
there are far fewer surplus coins to spend on Community Favour
(`favourCoinsToRepCost` = 200 coins → 1 reputation, unchanged on all presets),
and business/community-space `reputationPerTurn` values are unchanged. On
Medium, 69% of losses are now reputation collapses, against a PRD guardrail of
20–40% of losses ([prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md](docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md)
§G5 / guardrail table). Hard remains balanced at 48/52, which reads as a healthy
challenge spread — the distortion is Medium-specific.

## Users

- **Player** — wants losses to come from a mix of economic and reputational
  pressure, not a single dominant failure mode that makes the town feel
  impossible to keep alive.
  - *"As a player, I want reputation to recover at a pace that matches the
    slower coin economy, so that a run can be lost to bankruptcy or to
    reputation, not only to reputation."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants the documented loss-mode design intent
  restored and evidenced, with the win-rate ladder preserved.
  - *"As a designer, I want the Medium loss-mode split back inside the PRD
    band, backed by before/after Monte Carlo evidence and a reproducible
    commit SHA."*
- **Developer** — wants a small, reversible, card-data/config-only change with
  deterministic tests and no engine-rule churn.
  - *"As a developer, I want the reputation-source values and the loss-mode
    target asserted by tests so future rebalances cannot silently regress."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Before-state captured.** The after-five-turn-payback baseline is measured
   on the canonical profile (200 seeds, `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy;
   Easy/Medium/Hard) and recorded with its commit SHA: per-difficulty win
   rates and the Medium **loss-only** decomposition (reputation collapse /
   bankruptcy / other). Recorded in the work item.
2. **Evidence-led re-tune applied within the named levers.** Business and
   community-space `reputationPerTurn` and/or `favourCoinsToRepCost` (and, where
   evidenced, community-space reputation pricing) are adjusted in
   `src/card-data.csv` / `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`. **No engine-rule
   changes** (score formula, action economy, synergy formula, collapse
   threshold, discard reputation penalty are out of scope). Each changed value
   is justified against the measured loss decomposition.
3. **Target loss-mode mix achieved.** On the canonical profile after the
   changes, the Medium loss-only split meets the PRD band:
   - reputation collapse **20–40% of losses** (G5 target 30–40%);
   - bankruptcy **40–70% of losses** (G5 target 50–60%);
   and the primary balance gate holds: win-rate ladder
   `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`, with each difficulty inside its PRD win-rate band
   (Medium 20–85%, Easy 45–95%, Hard 5–60%).
4. **Before/after evidence recorded.** Before → after loss-mode decomposition
   and win rates per difficulty, with commit SHAs, are summarised in the work
   item **and** a `docs/main-street/` artefact. The committed baseline
   (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`) is regenerated **only** via
   the drift-report-then-ask workflow
   ([balance-guardrail-recommendations.md §0](docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md))
   with producer approval — never silently.
5. **Testing / validation.** At least one automated test asserts the tuned
   reputation-source invariants (e.g. the Community Favour rate and the
   reputation-generating card values), and the loss-mode target is captured by
   the balance metric output (G5) so a regression is detectable.
6. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Engine rules out of scope.** Per the parent's non-recommendations
  (score formula, action economy, synergy formula) — this is a parameter
  re-tune, not a rules change. The reputation-collapse threshold (`rep <= 0`)
  and the discard-cost reputation penalty are engine/rule behaviour and are
  not to be changed here.
- **Difficulty presets are unchanged** (parent decision Q3 = C); the win-rate
  ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` is the primary gate.
- **Do not raise `baseIncome`** — the five-turn payback contract
  (net payback 4.5–5.5 turns) must be preserved.
- **No new cards.** Use existing reputation sources only.
- **Evidence first.** Every parameter change must be justified by a measured
  before/after Monte Carlo run; the drift-report-then-ask workflow governs any
  committed-baseline regeneration.

## Existing state

**Reputation sources (current values, `src/card-data.csv` unless noted):**

- **Business `reputationPerTurn`** — 30 of 31 businesses carry it (e.g. Bakery
  +5, Café +10, Gallery/Spa/Private Clinic +25, Hotel +30, Clinic +40 with 0
  base income, Pawn Shop −10). Unchanged by the payback rebalance.
- **Community-space `reputationPerTurn`** — all 8: Park 0, Playground +5,
  Library/Garden/Fountain +10, Health Kiosk/Shelter +15, Public Art +20.
  These are the R4 (MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5) re-pricing candidates.
- **Community Favour** (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) — all three presets:
  `favourCoinsToRepCost = 200` coins → 1 rep; `favourRepToCoinsRepCost = 200`
  rep → `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain = 300` coins. Free, once per turn.
- **Positive events** — large one-shot `reputationDelta` on many events
  (e.g. `evt-charity-drive` +1350, `evt-volunteer-day` +1400, seasonal
  `evt-christmas` +650); negative events −100 each.
- **Storylines / upgrades** — `reputationBonus` on upgrade cards, storyline
  effects.

**Loss mechanic.** Reputation collapse fires when `resourceBank.reputation <= 0`
after turn 1 (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`). Loss-mode decomposition is
computed in `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` (G5) as
`lossesByMode[l] / totalLosses`.

**Design-intent bands (PRD §G5 / guardrail table):** bankruptcy 40–70% of
losses (target 50–60%); reputation collapse 20–40% of losses (target 30–40%);
timeout < 15%. Medium greedy win rate 20–85%.

**Current after-state (commit `8b8fe46`, [payback-rebalance-evidence.md](docs/main-street/payback-rebalance-evidence.md)):**
Medium win rate 0.325; loss-only split reputation collapse **69%** /
bankruptcy **30%** / other 1%. Hard 48/52.

**Greedy-AI caveat.** The greedy strategy scores `community-favour`
(`coins-to-rep`) at score **1** and treats it as a fallback that never
outranks a purchase (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` ~L1379). Changing
`favourCoinsToRepCost` alone may therefore not move greedy behaviour unless the
AI is stalled; passive `reputationPerTurn` is likely the primary lever.

## Desired change

Restore the Medium loss-mode split to the PRD band by re-tuning reputation
sources so reputation recovery keeps pace with the slower coin economy — a
card-data / config change, evidence-led and reversible, that preserves the
win-rate ladder and the five-turn payback contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — reputation source values: business / community-space
  `reputationPerTurn`, event `reputationDelta`, upgrade `reputationBonus`.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `favourCoinsToRepCost` /
  `favourRepToCoins*` per preset (if Community Favour is tuned).
- `src/scripts/generate-card-csv.ts` — CSV pipeline (if values are regenerated
  from templates).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — loss-mode decomposition (G5).
- `src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts` — `reputationCollapseRate_greedy_medium`
  band (currently defined but not enforced on the simulation).
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — design-intent
  win-rate bands.
- `tests/main-street/balance/` — balance metric tests.
- `docs/main-street/` — new before/after evidence artefact.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — coins-to-rep heuristic (out of scope unless a
  producer-approved scope decision is needed to make a lever effective).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — parent: five-turn payback rebalance and economy
  re-tune (in-progress). Source of the Q3 = C decision and constraint set.
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** — R1: re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI (sibling).
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** — R3: confirm win thresholds / run length as the
  difficulty lever (sibling; interacts with loss mix).
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — R4: re-price community spaces / events relative to
  slower business payback (sibling; **overlaps** community-space reputation
  pricing — coordinate to avoid conflicting edits).
- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** — R5: track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) post-rebalance.
- **MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL** — Add a charity shop (reputation-leaning Culture card;
  `reputationPerTurn = 15`, producer-set cost override).
- **MS-0MURC6XO8005W57D** — Closing a business damages reputation (interacts
  with reputation pressure).
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** — Visual representation of reputation (UI, out of scope).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — win-rate lift.** Reducing reputation-collapse losses raises the
  Medium win rate. The PRD band is wide (20–85%) and the ladder is the gate,
  but any move beyond the committed-baseline drift tolerance requires the
  drift-report-then-ask workflow and producer sign-off.
- **Risk — lever effectiveness.** The greedy AI scores coins-to-rep at 1, so
  `favourCoinsToRepCost` tuning alone may not change AI behaviour; the passive
  `reputationPerTurn` lever is likely decisive. If an AI-heuristic change is
  required, treat it as an explicit scope decision, not a silent edit.
- **Risk — overlap with R4.** Community-space/event re-pricing (R4) touches the
  same cards; sequence or coordinate to avoid conflicting edits.
- **Risk — overlap with R3.** Win thresholds / run length (R3) also shift the
  loss mix; changing both at once confounds attribution — land R2 first or
  measure independently.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Keep the change to reputation sources; do not
  rebalance upgrades, broad event economies, or add cards (record extra
  opportunities as linked work items).
- **Assumption.** The PRD loss-mode bands are authoritative; the target is
  reputation collapse 20–40% of Medium losses (G5 30–40%), bankruptcy
  40–70% (G5 50–60%).
- **Assumption.** Canonical profile = 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max
  turns, greedy strategy, Easy/Medium/Hard.
- **Assumption.** Card-data / config parameters are in scope; engine rules are
  not (per parent constraints).
- **Assumption.** The committed baseline is only regenerated via
  drift-report-then-ask with producer approval.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required — the design intent is documented in-repo.
The following were resolved by research (recorded for auditability):

- Q: What is a "healthy loss-mode mix"? — Answer (research): the PRD
  `prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` §G5 and guardrail table define
  reputation collapse 20–40% of losses (target 30–40%) and bankruptcy 40–70%
  (target 50–60%); Hard's 48/52 is described as "healthy" in the
  further-balancing artefact. Source:
  `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` L138–139, L507–514.
- Q: Which reputation sources are in scope? — Answer (research): the work-item
  AC names business `reputationPerTurn`, Community Favour
  (`favourCoinsToRepCost`), and community-space reputation cards; the parent's
  non-recommendations exclude engine-rule changes. Source: work-item
  description; `docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md` §6.
- Q: Is preserving the exact win rate required? — Answer (research): no — the
  primary gate is the ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`; the PRD win-rate bands
  (Medium 20–85%) and the drift-report-then-ask workflow govern acceptable
  movement. Source: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md`
  guardrail table; `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` §0.
## Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** – Track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) and placement dominance post-rebalance (open)

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.
- Unit tests for cost/extra effect application.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).

# Intake Brief: Greedy AI should spend less reputation on Community Favour

**Work item:** MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y · `bug` · `high`
**Discovered from:** observed greedy-AI behaviour on the post-payback-rebalance economy
**Related recommendation:** [further-balancing-recommendations.md §5 R2](docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md) / MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE (reputation re-tune)

## Headline

The greedy AI converts reputation into coins via Community Favour (`rep→coins`)
roughly **2–3.5 times per run** and **never** converts coins into reputation
(`coins→rep`), bleeding the reputation buffer that its own loss condition
(`reputation <= 0`) depends on. It should only exchange when the coins **enable
a profitable placement** and the timing/synergy value of that placement
justifies the reputation spent.

## Problem statement

Community Favour (`CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET`) is a free, once-per-turn exchange. The
greedy AI takes the `rep→coins` direction (200 reputation → 300 coins) whenever
its turn is *stalled* (it cannot afford the cheapest market card) and it holds a
single-reputation buffer — `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
(`scoreAction` → `case 'community-favour'`, and the competitive mirror
`competitiveFavourScore`). The check tests neither whether the gained coins
**buy anything profitable** nor whether the resulting placement carries enough
synergy/timing value to justify the reputation cost. Because reputation collapse
(`reputation <= 0` after turn 1) is a loss condition, the fallback trades a
loss-causing resource for liquidity the AI cannot turn into a win.

## Users

- **Player (single-player)** — wants an AI opponent/baseline that plays the
  economy sensibly and does not self-destruct by over-trading reputation for
  coins.
  - *"As a player, I want the greedy AI to look after its reputation, so that
    losses come from the economy, not from the AI repeatedly selling its
    reputation for coins it cannot use well."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants documented, measurable AI decision
  quality so balance conclusions drawn from greedy simulations remain valid.
  - *"As a designer, I want the greedy AI to use Community Favour only when it
    enables a profitable, well-synergised placement, backed by before/after
    evidence."*
- **Developer** — wants a small, well-tested heuristic change with deterministic
  unit tests, no engine-rule churn, and preserved balance guardrails.
  - *"As a developer, I want the favour heuristic and its guard rails pinned by
    tests so a future balance change cannot silently re-introduce the bleed."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** The current greedy behaviour is measured on the
   canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, all
   three difficulties) and recorded in the work item with its commit SHA:
   `rep→coins` uses per run, `coins→rep` uses per run, the reputation-collapse
   share of losses, and per-difficulty win rates. (Indicative 60-seed sample
   from intake research: `rep→coins` 3.52 / 3.12 / 2.18 uses per run on
   Easy/Medium/Hard; `coins→rep` 0; Medium reputation-collapse 29/39 losses ≈
   74%.)
2. **Enablement test added.** The `rep→coins` decision only fires when the
   coins gained (`favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`) actually **enable affording at
   least one card whose greedy placement value (`scoreBusinessAction` /
   `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, i.e. income + synergy over
   `aiPlanningHorizon`) is **positive after** the exchange. A stalled turn that
   would still be unable to afford a profitable card must **not** exchange.
3. **Value/timing gate added.** Among exchanges that pass AC2, the decision
   requires the enabled placement's reward (income + projected synergy over the
   remaining planning horizon) to clear a **named, documented threshold**
   relative to the reputation spent — so that only *early, high-value*
   placements (e.g. securing a strong synergy slot) justify the exchange. The
   threshold is a constant in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` and must be justified
   with the AC1/AC5 evidence.
4. **Reputation buffer preserved or strengthened.** The existing guard
   (reputation after the exchange stays `>= 1`) is retained; any strengthening
   (e.g. a larger post-exchange buffer) is explicit and tested.
5. **Before/after behaviour recorded.** On the canonical profile after the
   change, per-difficulty `rep→coins` uses per run are **materially lower** than
   the AC1 baseline and the Medium reputation-collapse share of losses **does
   not increase**, while the primary balance gate holds: the win-rate ladder
   `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` and the committed-baseline tolerances (`winRate
   ±0.25`, `coins ±30%`; [monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts](tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts)).
   Before/after figures and commit SHAs are recorded in the work item and a
   `docs/main-street/` artefact. If any committed-baseline drift beyond
   tolerance is required, follow the drift-report-then-ask workflow — never
   regenerate the baseline silently.
6. **Testing / validation.** Automated tests in
   `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` (extended) or a dedicated
   test file pin the new decision: exchange **declined** when it would not
   enable a profitable placement; exchange **declined** when the enabled
   placement is not early/high-value; exchange **taken** when it enables a
   high-value early synergy placement; the reputation-buffer guard; and
   deterministic selection. Existing Community Favour AI tests are updated to
   the new contract rather than deleted.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries (in particular `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` and the
   Community Favour move-evaluation notes).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No engine-rule changes** — Community Favour costs/gains
  (`favourCoinsToRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsRepCost`,
  `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`), the action economy, the score formula, the synergy
  formula, and the `reputation <= 0` collapse threshold are **out of scope**.
  This is a heuristic change only (confirmed by intake research measuring that
  parameter-only tuning did not move greedy behaviour — MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE).
- **No card-data rebalance.** Reputation sources/Pricing are owned by R2
  (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE) and R4 (MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5); do not change
  `src/card-data.csv` here.
- **Preserve determinism.** Same seed + same state → same decision.
- **Preserve the win-rate ladder.** The primary balance gate is
  `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`; the change must not invert it.
- **Evidence first.** Every threshold introduced must be justified against the
  measured before/after behaviour; the committed baseline is regenerated only
  via the drift-report-then-ask workflow with producer approval.

## Existing state

**Decision site.** `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`:

- `scoreAction` → `case 'community-favour'` (~L1363): `coins→rep` always scores
  `1`; `rep→coins` scores `3` when
  `coins < getCheapestMarketCost(state)` **and**
  `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost + 1`, otherwise `1`.
- `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 9 (~L960): takes the best favour action only
  when its score is `> 1` — i.e. effectively only the `rep→coins` fallback. A
  `coins→rep` action is therefore **never** taken (score `1`).
- `competitiveFavourScore` (~L1981) encodes the **same** stalled+buffer rule for
  `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`; its priority chain likewise takes favour only
  when `score > 1` (~L2145).

**Why the current gate is too loose.** `getCheapestMarketCost` includes *every*
market family (staff/events included) and the reward of the placement is not
considered at all. A stalled AI will exchange 200 reputation for 300 coins even
when the only affordable card is value-negative (e.g. Pawn Shop, which carries
`reputationPerTurn = -10`) or has no synergy.

**Measured current behaviour (60-seed intake sample, greedy, commit `dev` HEAD
at intake time).** The AI takes `rep→coins` several times per run and never
takes `coins→rep`:

| Difficulty | `rep→coins` uses/run | `coins→rep` uses/run | win rate | rep-collapse / bankruptcy losses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Easy   | 3.52 | 0 | 0.650 | 15 / 6 |
| Medium | 3.12 | 0 | 0.350 | 29 / 10 |
| Hard   | 2.18 | 0 | 0.117 | 26 / 27 |

**Loss condition.** Reputation collapse fires when
`resourceBank.reputation <= 0` after turn 1
(`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`).

**Existing tests.** `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` currently
pins the *old* contract, including
`scores coins-to-rep at the low default` and
`scores rep-to-coins above the default when cash-strapped with rep to spare`, so
it must be updated alongside the heuristic (AC6).

## Desired change

Replace the "stalled + any buffer" `rep→coins` heuristic with an
**enablement + value/timing** heuristic: exchange reputation for coins only when
the coins buy a **profitable** placement **and** the placement's reward (income
+ synergy over the remaining horizon) is **significant enough, early enough**
(e.g. securing a strong synergy slot) to justify the reputation spent. Keep the
reputation-buffer guard. Apply the same rule to the competitive mirror so the
two heuristics cannot diverge.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `scoreAction` `community-favour` case, the
  `rep→coins` enablement/value helper, `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 9,
  and `competitiveFavourScore` (competitive mirror).
- `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` — update existing contract
  tests and add the new enablement/value/timing cases.

  move-evaluation heuristic.

  if a reputation-collapse metric needs surfacing for the evidence artefact.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — R2: re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin
  economy (open, `plan_complete`, producer question pending). **Coordinates:**
  R2 tunes card-data reputation values to move the Medium loss-mode split into
  the PRD band; this item changes *AI decision quality* and must not double-count
  the same outcome. R2's implementation comment explicitly measured that
  `favourCoinsToRepCost` tuning does not move greedy behaviour — corroborating
  that this fix belongs in the AI heuristic.
- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — parent of R2: five-turn payback rebalance
  (in-progress). Source of the tighter-economy design intent.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — R4: re-price community spaces and events (completed);
  touches community-space reputation pricing — out of scope here.
- **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** — "Bank your spare action is a dead end in the
  tutorial" (open): also concerns the `rep→coins` fallback as a stall-breaker.
- **CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET** — original Community Favour implementation (free
  once-per-turn exchange) and the `avgCoinsPerTurn` guardrail widening that
  recorded the `rep→coins` fallback's liquidity contribution.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** — BankingGreedyStrategy: introduces
  `aiPlanningHorizon`, the horizon helper this heuristic will reuse, and the
  precedent for difficulty-scaled AI aggressiveness.
- **MS-0MUWKG6NS006OG2D** — "Community Garden should be Entertainment"
  (completed): community-space card data (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — stall/win-rate regression.** Removing the free fallback means more
  end-turns when the AI cannot afford a profitable card. This is the intended
  trade-off, but Medium/Hard win rates could fall; the ladder and committed
  tolerances must still hold (AC5). Mitigation: measure before/after and treat
  any out-of-tolerance drift as a producer decision.
- **Risk — threshold over-fitting.** A value/timing threshold tuned to the
  200-seed canonical set may not generalise. Mitigation: keep it a single named
  constant, document its derivation, and pin behaviour with unit tests rather
  than only the stochastic guardrail.
- **Risk — overlap with R2.** R2 also targets the reputation-collapse share of
  losses; changing both at once confounds attribution. Mitigation: this item's
  primary ACs are behavioural (usage + enablement), and any loss-mode claim is
  reported alongside R2's state rather than asserted as this item's alone.
- **Risk — competitive divergence.** If only the single-player heuristic is
  changed, `competitiveFavourScore` keeps the loose rule. Mitigation: apply the
  shared helper to both (decision recorded as an assumption below).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Do not rebalance Community Favour parameters, cards,
  or the collapse threshold; record extra opportunities as linked work items.
- **Assumption.** Scope is the greedy AI heuristic (single-player
  `scoreAction`); the competitive mirror is updated with the same helper to
  prevent divergence, but competitive-specific tuning is out of scope.
- **Assumption.** "Profitable card" means a legal placement whose greedy score
  (`scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, value − effective
  cost) is `> 0` after the exchange.
- **Assumption.** "Early brings significant value" is represented by
  `aiPlanningHorizon(state)` and the projected synergy bonus — the same horizon
  helper the banking heuristic uses.
- **Assumption.** Canonical profile = 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max
  turns, greedy, Easy/Medium/Hard.
- **Assumption.** The committed baseline is regenerated only via the
  drift-report-then-ask workflow with producer approval.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking producer questions were required — the seed intent is specific and
the remaining decisions were resolved by repo research and a measurement run.
Records (for auditability; idempotent, do not duplicate on re-run):

- Q: Does "using Community Favour to get money" mean `rep→coins` or
  `coins→rep`? — Answer (research): `rep→coins` (200 reputation → 300 coins).
  Measured 60-seed greedy sample shows `rep→coins` used 2.18–3.52×/run and
  `coins→rep` used 0×; only `rep→coins` drains the loss-causing resource.
  Source: `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` `scoreAction`; intake evidence script.
- Q: Is the fix a parameter re-tune (like R2) or an AI-heuristic change? —
  Answer (research): AI-heuristic. R2's implementation comment records that
  reducing `favourCoinsToRepCost` to 10/20/50/100 moved the Medium loss split by
  <2 pp — parameters do not move greedy behaviour. Source: MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE
  implementation comment.
- Q: What is a "profitable card"? — Answer (research): a legal placement whose
  greedy score (income + projected synergy over `aiPlanningHorizon`, minus
  effective cost) is positive. Source: `scoreBusinessAction`,
  `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, `aiPlanningHorizon` in
  `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`.
- Q: Should the competitive AI heuristic change too? — Answer (producer):
  **yes** — both `scoreAction` and `competitiveFavourScore` encode the same
  stalled+buffer rule; apply the shared enablement/value helper to both (via a
  common function) to avoid divergence. Competitive-specific tuning remains out
  of scope. Source: producer reply, 2026-10-06.
- Q: Should this item target the PRD loss-mode band (rep collapse 20–40% of
  Medium losses) as a hard gate? — Answer (producer): **no** — the primary gate
  is behavioural (usage/enablement) plus the win-rate ladder and
  committed-baseline tolerances; the loss-mode band remains owned by R2
  (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE) via card-data, and changing both confounds attribution.
  Source: producer reply, 2026-10-06.

### Questions resolved

Both producer questions were answered on 2026-10-06: (1) competitive mirror —
**yes**, apply the shared helper; (2) loss-mode band hard gate — **no**. No open
questions remain.

**Parent:** MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL (Competitive game ends on AI seat failure)

## Goal

Align the competitive Monte-Carlo harness with per-seat attribution,
elimination and last-standing winner resolution, and re-baseline the seeded
deterministic assertions that were previously masked by the defect.

## Context

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts:836-845` already attributes the loss reason per
  player from that player's own wallet — evidence the intended semantics are
  per-seat, but the engine set a global loss.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts:70` swapped seed
  `'ac1-cap-1'` (ended via `reputation_collapse`) for `'ac1-cap-3'` as a
  workaround — see MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN / MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Monte-Carlo harness consumes the per-seat failure evaluation and
   elimination state, and reports elimination/last-standing outcomes
   consistently with the engine.
2. The previously-worked-around seed assertion (`'ac1-cap-1'`) is either
   re-enabled with the corrected expectation, or the reason it remains
   swapped is documented in the test with a reference to the parent item.
3. A determinism regression test runs the same seed twice and asserts
   identical per-seat outcomes (winner, eliminations, end reason).
4. Monte-Carlo runs remain bounded by `maxTurns`; no seed regresses into a

5. Aggregated Monte-Carlo statistics no longer attribute one seat's collapse
